title: History 16: What open means: weights, licences and the ecosystem

questions.q: According to the lesson's ship analogy, what does the 'licence' represent in relation to a model?
options: The flag it flies and the laws of the sea it must obey
questions.answer: The flag it flies and the laws of the sea it must obey
questions.why: The lesson states: 'The licence is the flag it flies and the laws of the sea it must obey.'

questions.q: In the transparency scoring system, what is the formula for the Reproducibility Score?
questions.why: The lesson defines the Reproducibility Score as: Reproducibility Score = 1 / (1 + σ²), where σ² is the variance of T.

questions.q: What are the two conditions required for a model to be considered a true 'open ecosystem' according to the defined mechanism?
questions.answer: The average transparency (T_bar) must be greater than the threshold (tau), AND all individual component scores (t_i) must be greater than or equal to the minimum component score (t_min).
questions.why: The lesson states: 'is_open = (T_bar > tau) AND all_components_open = (forall i, t_i >= t_min)'.

questions.q: Which function in ComfyUI is identified as the primary entry point for loading checkpoints and detecting model architecture?
questions.why: The lesson states: 'The function load_checkpoint_guess_config in comfy/sd.py is the primary entry point.'

questions.q: Why is it a common mistake to assume that 'open' code implies the model is fully usable without checking other components?
options: Because open code always requires proprietary weights to run
Because the weights might be proprietary or have restrictive licences even if the code is open
Because open code cannot be modified by the community
Because the text encoder is always closed-source
questions.answer: Because the weights might be proprietary or have restrictive licences even if the code is open
questions.why: The lesson notes: 'Many models have open-source code... but the weights are proprietary. You cannot run the model without the weights. Always check the weight file's licence.'
